title: Existence of the q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs
abstract: For every integer q at least 3, the formalization proves the existence of a limiting q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs. A single constant alpha_q in [1/2, log(q)/log(q/(q-1))] gives the transition for the uniform model with floor(c n) edges and the transition at d = 2 alpha_q for the binomial model with edge probability d/n. For every fixed eta in (0,1), there is C > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, the first loss of q-colorability under independent uniform additions of unordered pairs of distinct vertices lies within C n (log n)^(-3/2) steps of deterministic integer centers with probability at least 1-eta. The centers divided by n converge to the same alpha_q. Repeated edges are retained in this process. The scope is Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 of the included manuscript.
